title: European Commission hit by cyberattack affecting staff payroll and leave systems
date_note: Date of the report; Politico, relayed by Izvestia, says the attack had been going on for more than 10 days.
summary: Euronews and Politico report an attack on the European Commission, detected 22 October; per Politico (via Security Affairs) systems were disrupted for more than ten days. Sysper and MyPMO were taken offline and later restored. Security Affairs says CERT-EU identified the AI pentest tool ARTEX as a possible tool; that is suspected, not confirmed. Scope remains unclear.
plain: The European Commission says some of its internal systems were attacked and some applications were switched off. Most staff were paid as usual, but some could not file time sheets or arrange leave.
exec: An attack on an EU institution's HR systems puts staff personal data at risk.
action: If you work with EU institutions, expect notices from them and treat unexpected messages claiming to be from Commission staff with care.
impact: Sysper (pay statements, leave, time tracking) and MyPMO (medical reimbursement) taken offline, restored early in the week of 16 Nov (heise); salaries paid as usual; data exposure not established.

sources.name: The Telegraph via Yahoo News (relaying Politico)

validation.note: Euronews (own anonymous official; Sysper and JSIS named) and Politico (relayed by Izvestia, Telegraph, Anadolu, La Libre) report independently; the Commission has not confirmed the scope. Politico original not read. 20 Nov: Security Affairs (19 Nov) reports CERT-EU named ARTEX as a possible tool and more than ten days of disruption; CERT-EU and Politico originals not read.

review.note: Compared with heise, Euronews, AP/WRAL, Newsweek, CSO, Izvestia: Sysper re-crash was Wednesday 18 Nov not 19 Nov (fixed); merged sources from duplicate record; salaries as usual and 10+ days match Izvestia relaying Politico
